description: Executes an endpoint found via search_endpoints. Pass `routeId` and `arguments` (keys = `parameters[].name` of that route, omit if the route has none). Flow: if you have a balance (see `top_up_balance`) and it covers the route price, pass `buyerID` next to `routeId`  (not inside arguments - that object is forwarded to the endpoint) - payment is taken from balance, no 402 challenge, so it is much faster. Otherwise the first call WITHOUT a payment signature returns isError=true with `x402Version`+`accepts` in structuredContent - sign those accepts and retry with `_meta["x402/payment"]` (base64 payload); a partial balance still yields a 402 for the shortfall. Other isError cases: `invalid_arguments` (structuredContent.details[]/requiredArgs[] tell what to fix and retry), `route_unresolved` (pick another routeId from plan[]), `failed` (refunded/refundTx; try another route). On success, returns the actual result of the endpoint. No auth. Limits (per IP): paid 300/5min, burst 200/10s, total 1000/15min. Tip: see the `top_up_balance` tool description to learn how to speed up processing of your calls via balance.

arguments.description: Endpoint arguments. Keys = `parameters[].name` of the chosen route. Example: `parameters[] = [{name:"address", in:"path", required:true}]` → `{ "address": "0x098B…" }`.

buyerID.description: Optional 16-char buyer ID (meta.yourID from any paid response). Pass it in the first call next to `routeId` to skip the 402 challenge: if the balance covers the route price, payment is taken from balance (no on-chain signature, so it is much faster). If the balance is partial, you still get 402 for the shortfall - sign and retry with _meta["x402/payment"].

name: call_endpoint
